To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the marine microalga Nannochloropsis gaditana contains molecules that are able to alter the microtubules network of mammalian cells and that can be solubilized in an aqueous solution by using a polymer.

we have identified three bioactive compounds from the microalga N. gaditena, which can affect microtubule cytoskeleton and that we have demonstrated that a phtalate and a pigment can alter the morphology of HeLa cell and that a phtalat can alter microtubule polymerization.

1) the lipids and pigments from N. gaditena can affect the microtubule cytoskeleton and 2) the phtalates from N. gaditenas have a direct effect on the microtubules of mammalian cells and 3) the solubilisation of phtalate and pheophorbides using the polymer pMeOx allows to reduce the concentrations needed to induce the same effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extraction, purification and characterization of natural bioactive molecules isolated from the microalga N. gaditane.
the isolation and characterization of bioactive molecules from marine microalgae.
the isolation and purification of biologically active substances extracted from the microalga N. gaditena and their impact on mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microalgal species N. gaditanna is a promising source of molecules bioactive for the development of new anti-proliferative agents.
the microalgae are a source of bioactive molecules with potential antiproliferative and/or anticancer activity.
the microalga N. gaditena is a rich source of bioactive molecules which could be of interest in the development of anti-proliferative and anticancer drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the marine diatom N. gaditena contains a wide range of bioactive molecules which can be isolated and used to inhibit cell division in mammal cells.
we have isolated and identified bioactive compounds from microalgae N. gaditanea that can act on the cytoskeleton of mammalian cells and more specifically on the microtubules network.
we have demonstrated the presence of bioactive molecules in the microalgae N. gaditanna and their effect on the cytoskeleton and more particularly on the microtubules network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microalga N. gaditena can be used as an original source for bioactive molecules with antiproliferative and anticancer activities and that the use of biotechnological process can improve the efficiency of these bioactive molecules.
the marine microalgae Nannochloropsis gaditana contains bioactive molecules that can alter the cytoskeleton in mammalian cell cultures and that could be of interest for anticancer drug development.
the use of marine microalgae as source of bioactive molecules is a promising strategy for the discovery of new molecules with anticancer properties.
